fetch_policy_note: This manifest is a committed local snapshot of upstream references. DARE Agent Security performs no network fetch of standards at validation time, and Cycle 016 contacts no memory store, cache, database, vector store or SaaS memory provider. Canonical references are recorded for attribution and traceability only.
conformance_disclaimer: DARE claims no conformance with any memory, storage, retrieval or context-management specification. Cycle 016 models persisted memory declaratively because that shape is useful for deterministic comparison, not because the engine implements or is certified against any specification. Resemblance of a data model is not conformance, and a draft or proposal referenced here stays a draft or proposal.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
sources.mapping_notes: ASI06 Memory and Context Poisoning is the risk-family parent for Cycle 016. DARE properties are narrower, deterministically decidable security invariants and are not one-to-one restatements of ASI06.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications 2025
sources.mapping_notes: LLM01 Prompt Injection and LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses are adjacent. Cycle 016 is distinguished from LLM01 by persistence and recall, and deliberately does not implement the vector/embedding surface, which belongs to Cycle 017.

sources.title: DARE Cycle 013 — Prompt Injection Security
sources.mapping_notes: Cycle 016 reuses the rule that untrusted data does not become an authoritative instruction. It does not reuse or duplicate the prompt-injection evaluator; the distinguishing feature here is that the untrusted data was persisted and later recalled.

sources.title: DARE Cycle 015 — Identity, Privilege and Delegation Security
sources.mapping_notes: Cycle 016 reuses principal and tenant conventions and sanitized-identifier rules so a memory boundary aligns with identity semantics rather than redefining them. It does not reuse the identity evaluator.

sources.title: Memory provenance and recall-authority binding
sources.mapping_notes: The rule that recalled memory carries no more authority than its source trust class and authorized objective is a DARE modelling position, recorded as an open proposal rather than as an established standard.

sources.title: DARE Cycle 016 — Memory and Context Poisoning Security
sources.mapping_notes: This cycle's own design, blueprint and acceptance criteria.

memory_trust_statement.recall_rule: recall is not permission to influence
memory_trust_statement.storage_rule: Persisting data does not convert that data into authority. Untrusted memory may exist as data without producing a violation; a violation requires deterministic evidence that it exceeded its authorized boundary.
memory_trust_statement.promotion_rule: Trust elevation must be machine-readable and policy-derived. Content cannot promote itself by carrying words such as system, admin or verified.

surface_classes.title: Memory provenance
surface_classes.description: Whether persisted memory retains machine-readable source and provenance before it influences behavior.

surface_classes.title: Memory write trust boundary
surface_classes.description: Whether untrusted content silently became trusted or policy-authoritative persisted memory.

surface_classes.title: Principal, tenant and namespace isolation
surface_classes.description: Whether memory crossed a principal, tenant or namespace boundary on write, recall or influence.

surface_classes.title: Memory lifecycle validity
surface_classes.description: Whether expired or revoked memory influenced a later decision, evaluated on deterministic logical time.

surface_classes.title: Recall-to-decision influence
surface_classes.description: Whether recalled memory altered the authorized objective, tool selection, tool arguments or a protected field beyond policy.

property_mappings.notes: Pre-existing since Cycle 012. Cycle 016 adds specialized properties beside it and leaves its identifier, wording and applicability unchanged.
Pre-existing since Cycle 012. Cycle 016 aligns its memory tenant checks with Cycle 015 tenant conventions rather than redefining this property.
Narrower than ASI06: memory must retain machine-readable source and provenance before it influences behavior.

property_mappings.reference: untrusted data is not an authoritative instruction
property_mappings.notes: Applies the Cycle 013 untrusted-data rule to persistence: untrusted content may be stored as data but must not silently become policy-authoritative memory.

property_mappings.reference: recalled memory carries no more authority than its source trust class
property_mappings.notes: A DARE modelling position recorded as an open proposal: recalled memory carries no more authority than its source trust class and authorized objective.
Narrower than ASI06: expired or revoked memory must not influence a later decision, evaluated on deterministic logical time.

explicitly_out_of_scope.topic: Vector retrieval, embedding similarity, document chunk authorization and RAG corpus isolation
explicitly_out_of_scope.note: Cycle 016 validates persisted memory and context state. It implements no embedding retrieval, similarity search, vector-store authorization or cross-document retrieval testing.

explicitly_out_of_scope.topic: OAuth, OIDC, JWT verification, JWKS, live identity providers, policy decision points and token exchange
explicitly_out_of_scope.note: Cycle 016 parses and verifies no token and contacts no identity or authorization service.

inherited_lessons.lesson: Credential detection must match token shape, not the words used to discuss credentials, so that an honest description of the boundary stays writable.
Key material spans multiple whitespace-separated lines; masking that stops at the first whitespace leaves the key body in retained text.
Control characters and bidi overrides in identifiers reach reports and logs, so values are swept as well as field names.
A fixture that can state its own outcome makes the evaluator ceremonial; the expected outcome lives in the test, never in the fixture.
A corpus test must prove every invariant is reachable in both the passing and the failing direction rather than assuming it.
A safety-control test whose condition is impossible by construction asserts nothing; the control must be observably able to trip.
Every invariant declares the observation channels it needs, and a missing channel yields INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS.
Violations are collected as a list; one classification never masks another.
